ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Financial Transaction Reports Act (FTRA), Act No. 16319 as amended through 2024, arts. 5, 5-2 and 5-4; FTRA Enforcement Decree arts. 10-12; Financial Services Commission/Korean Financial Intelligence Unit Customer Identification and Verification Regulation (KoFIU Directive 2024-3); Proceeds of Crime Act; Act on the Regulation and Punishment of Criminal Proceeds Concealment; Act on the Prohibition of Financing of Offences Implying Public Reprisal and the Proliferation of Weapons of Mass Destruction; Korean Commercial Act arts. 288 through 300 (Chusik Hoesa).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation / Certified Registry Extract of each corporate shareholder and UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registry of Commerce under the Supreme Court of Korea or the competent company registrar in the jurisdiction of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille route for Hague Convention states: certification by the issuing registry followed by Apostille from the state's designated competent authority. Consular route for non-member states: certification by the issuing registry followed by legalization by the Republic of Korea's diplomatic or consular mission. The two routes are mutually exclusive and must not be chained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of Existence of each corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent corporate registry or licensing authority in the jurisdiction of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille route: issuance by the registry, then Apostille by the designated competent authority in the same country. Consular route: issuance by the registry, then legalization by the Korean consulate with jurisdiction over the issuing authority. Never combine a Convention apostille with consular authentication.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Irrevocable Power of Attorney authorizing the incorporation of the Korean Chusik Hoesa
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors and notary public in the jurisdiction of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille route: notarized board resolution, then Apostille by the state's competent authority. Consular route: notarized board resolution, then Korean consulate legalization. Parallel alternatives only; do not chain an Apostille and consular legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Articles of Association / Constitutional Documents of the corporate shareholder and any intermediary holding entities
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public or company registry in the jurisdiction of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague route: notary or registry certification, followed by Apostille by the issuing state's competent authority. Non-Hague route: notary or registry certification, followed by legalization at the Korean embassy or consulate. Use one path exclusively.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter for the shareholder and each UBO covering creditworthiness, ownership of funds, and compliance record
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Branch manager or compliance officer of the principal bank in the jurisdiction of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille route: bank statement notarized if required by the jurisdictional convention, then Apostille by the competent authority. Consular route: bank statement notarized, then Korean consular legalization. The two paths are alternatives and must not be used sequentially.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Every shareholder, UBO, director, officer, authorized signatory, and connected intermediary must be screened before filing. Screening must cover the UN Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN and OFAC non-SDN sectoral lists, EU and UK consolidated financial sanctions lists, Interpol notices, Korean FSS/KoFIU watchlists, and adverse media databases. Each individual must be checked for PEP status covering immediate family and close associates; any foreign PEP or Korean public official triggers enhanced due diligence, source-of-funds evidence, senior-management approval, and ongoing transaction monitoring. Automated name-matching must be supplemented by manual review to resolve false positives and residual risk.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court of Korea Corporate Registry Online Name Search and Reservation Portal (HUKS) available through the Korean Internet Registration Office
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The statutory name of a Chusik Hoesa must be written in Korean Hangul. A foreign-language name may be registered as a trade name but not as the statutory registrable name for Korean public filing. Name clearance applies the four-tier comparison doctrine: identical Hangul spelling, phonetic identity after Hanja or foreign-language transliteration, homophonic equivalence, and overall visual or impression similarity in the relevant geographic scope. The corporate suffix demonstrating stock-company form is mandatory and must appear in the complete name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: An applicant may request one extension of the 30-day name reservation through the HUKS portal before expiry, but the extension is discretionary and a new search fee is charged. If the registry rejects the proposed name, the applicant must obtain the official rejection notice and file a written objection within 14 days to the registration division of the district court with jurisdiction over the registered office, attaching a fresh name-search certificate, the proposed Hangul and transliterated forms, and any ministerial approvals for sensitive tokens. If the court dismisses the objection, the applicant may pursue administrative adjudication through the Court Administration Office or administrative litigation within 90 days, or simply file a new reservation with a distinctive differentiating token.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: For a commercial 3D animation and VFX producer, a bare virtual office, commercial mailbox, or PO-box address will not satisfy the National Tax Service place-of-business requirement and will be treated as a red flag by Korean commercial banks for corporate bank account opening. The registered address must be a demonstrable physical establishment with the statutory nameplate, production workstations, 3D software licenses, client contracts, operational records, and staff presence. A serviced office that provides a dedicated executive room, Korean-language signage, conference facilities, and a full-service lease can be acceptable, but mail-only forwarding is not.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk: 25%-35% likelihood of an unannounced National Tax Service or municipal registry field inspection within the first 12 months. Checklist: statutory nameplate on the door, original or certified physical lease of at least one year, occupied workstations, 3D animation/VFX software licenses, render farm or cloud computing subscription in the legal-entity name, production samples, signed client agreements, payroll and social-insurance records, VAT invoices, corporate bank statements showing operating expenditures, and a clear separation from any virtual-address supplier.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Act No. 1000, as amended), Book III, Articles 289 through 317; specifically Article 289 (Articles of Incorporation), Article 295 (subscription and payment for shares at incorporation), Article 302 (election of directors and statutory officers at incorporation), Article 317 (registration of incorporation), and Article 363 (post-incorporation governance filings and officer registrations)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commercial Registration Division, Registration Bureau of the district court having jurisdiction over the head office; for Seoul, this is the Registration Division of the Seoul Central District Court, administered under the Supreme Court of Korea
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of Incorporation of a Stock Company (prescribed court form under the Registration of Real Estate and Corporations Rules) together with the notarized Articles of Incorporation as the principal statutory exhibit
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None: the Korean Commercial Act does not impose a statutory minimum paid-up share capital for a Chusik Hoesa. However, all issued share subscription money must be fully paid into a blocked subscription deposit account at a Korean financial institution before submission of the incorporation registration application. The deposited funds remain blocked until the court registry issues the Certificate of Registered Matters. For non-resident shareholders, the remittance into Korea must be reported under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and kept traceable as investment money; the deposit receipt from the bank is a mandatory registry exhibit.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS RESOLUTION OF [COMPANY NAME], A CHUSIK HOESA PROVISIONALLY INCORPORATED UNDER THE COMMERCIAL ACT OF THE REPUBLIC OF KOREA

RESOLVED, that the formation of this Chusik Hoesa, as evidenced by the notarized Articles of Incorporation executed by the incorporators on [date] and to be filed at the Commercial Registration Division of the competent district court, is hereby ratified, adopted, and approved in its entirety. The corporate name is [Company Name] (Chusik Hoesa); the registered head office is at [full address in Seoul or other Korean jurisdiction]; and the principal business object is the commercial production of 3D animation, CGI visual effects, character animation, post-production, content distribution, and related consulting services classified under ISIC 5911 and NAICS 512110. The full business object clause has been incorporated into the Articles of Incorporation and is declared lawful under Korean commercial, media, and digital content statutes, and it does not require any physical manufacturing, chemical, assembly, or warehousing license.

RESOLVED FURTHER, that the subscription and share capital arrangement approved by the incorporators, consisting of [number] subscribed shares with par value of [Korean won] per share and aggregate paid-in capital of [Korean won], is hereby confirmed. All paid-in amounts have been deposited into a blocked corporate formation deposit account at [bank name] in the Republic of Korea as a condition precedent to registration. The board authorizes the representative director to release such blocked funds immediately upon issuance of the certificate of registered matters by the court registry, and to apply the funds exclusively to lawful corporate purposes, including operating costs, payroll, tax deposits, and production expenses. Since the Korean Commercial Act imposes no minimum statutory capital for a stock company, the subscribed capital is valid; any non-resident subscription remittances shall be supported by proper foreign exchange declarations.

RESOLVED FURTHER, that the banking and payment infrastructure of the Company is established as follows. The board approves the opening and operation of corporate bank accounts at [bank name], and designates the representative director alone, or jointly with any other director, as authorized signatories for all accounts, including receipt of client payments through Wise B2B and SWIFT wire transfers, disbursement of project fees, payment of subcontractors, wage payments, statutory social insurance contributions, and settlement of corporate tax liabilities. The registered head office is adopted as the Company's exclusive operating address and legal seat, and the board confirms that no heavy industrial facility, warehouse, chemical plant, or assembly line is required for the registered object.

RESOLVED FURTHER, that the statutory officers of the Company are formally appointed and authorized as follows: [Name 1] as sole representative director and chief executive officer; [Name 2] as director or auditor to the extent required by the Articles of Incorporation; and [Name 3] as corporate secretary and authorized filer before the court registry and the National Tax Service. Each appointed officer shall sign the required statutory acceptance forms and register his or her office in the court registry as mandatory under the Commercial Act. All officers shall observe fiduciary duties, conflict-of-interest rules, and confidentiality obligations, and shall act only within the object clauses contained in the Articles of Incorporation.

RESOLVED FURTHER, that the board adopts a full corporate governance and compliance program, including anti-money laundering client due diligence, verification of beneficial owners for bank and payment-rail compliance, data privacy protocols under the Personal Information Protection Act, labor and social insurance registration for Korean employees, and value-added tax invoicing controls. The representative director and corporate secretary are jointly and severally delegated to execute all registration application forms, pay official fees, obtain the Business Registration Certificate from the National Tax Service, open the corporate bank accounts, report the corporate seal, register employees, and complete any ancillary filings required for the lawful commencement of digital 3D animation and VFX production activities in the Republic of Korea.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation, Notarization, and Execution of the Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public appointed in the Republic of Korea; selected by the incorporators under the Notary Public Act
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Company counsel prepares the Korean-language Articles of Incorporation in full compliance with Commercial Act Article 289. Every incorporator, or an attorney-in-fact with a notarized power of attorney, must execute the Articles before a notary public. The Articles must set out the corporate name, head-office address, business object limited to CGI, 3D animation, visual effects and related services under ISIC 5911, total authorized shares, issue price of subscribed shares, amount paid in per share, method of public notice, names of incorporators, and appointment or election method of directors and auditor. The notary certifies the execution by issuing a notarial certificate and affixing the seal; at least one original is retained for submission to the court registry.
required_dossiers: Passport or alien registration card of each incorporator
Notarized power of attorney if a proxy executes
Completed draft Articles of Incorporation in Korean
Statement of incorporation purpose and business scope
Proof of head-office address, such as lease agreement or right-to-use certificate
Identity documents for all directors and the auditor nominated in the Articles
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary public refuses certification because of an omitted statutory particular, the drafting counsel cures the omission by amending the Articles, re-executing all incorporator signatures, and obtaining a fresh notarial certificate. If a signature is defective, the affected incorporator must re-sign or execute a new notarized power of attorney; this correction is completed within one additional SLA day.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital Subscription, Blocked Deposit, and Korean Bank Deposit Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Domestic Korean financial institution licensed under the Banking Act; foreign exchange reporting to the bank or the Ministry of Economy and Finance designated foreign exchange information system where inbound remittance occurs
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Each incorporator executes a share subscription form stating the number of shares, per-share issuance price, total amount subscribed, and the subscription date. The company opens a provisional blocked account under the intended corporate name or representative incorporator name, and all subscription proceeds are remitted into that account. The bank verifies the identity of each subscriber, performs FATCA and CRS due diligence, and issues a certificate of paid-in capital deposit to be later attached to the incorporation application. The funds must remain blocked until the registry grants incorporation. For foreign subscribers, inbound wire remittances must be accompanied by a deposit purpose code showing share subscription, and the bank must issue a foreign exchange receipt or certificate.
required_dossiers: Executed share subscription forms
Notarized Articles of Incorporation or a certified copy
Passport or alien registration card of each subscribing incorporator
Bank-mandated FATCA/CRS and beneficial owner certification forms
Remittance instructions and SWIFT or wire receipts
Provisional account opening application and board or incorporators' instruction
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank rejects a remittance due to mismatched subscriber names, missing source-of-funds documentation, or sanctions-screening issues, the filing attorney obtains corrected wire instructions from the remitter and re-executes the subscription form with the exact legal name. If anti-money laundering review is extended, the company furnishes a source-of-wealth statement; the blocked deposit certificate is then reissued and the step is closed within two SLA days of cure.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Statutory Incorporation Registration at the District Court Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registration Division of the district court with territorial jurisdiction over the registered head office; in Seoul, the Commercial Registration Division of the Seoul Central District Court
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within the statutory window after completion of the subscription payment, the incorporators submit the application for incorporation registration under Commercial Act Article 317. The filing must attach the original notarized Articles of Incorporation, the bank-issued paid-in capital deposit certificate, each director's and auditor's signed acceptance of office, a statement that all shares have been subscribed and paid, and evidence of the head-office proper site, such as a lease agreement or floor plan. The registry clerk examines substantive and formal legality, verifies the corporate object and statutory particulars, and assesses registration tax. Upon approval, the court issues an extract of the corporate register (certificate of registered matters), thereby perfecting the legal existence of the Chusik Hoesa.
required_dossiers: Prescribed application for incorporation registration
Original notarized Articles of Incorporation
Bank certificate confirming paid-in capital deposit
Written acceptance of office from each director and auditor
Incorporators' statutory statement certifying completion of subscriptions
Proof of head office, including lease contract and owner's registration certificate
Registration tax payment receipt
Corporate seal report form and specimen seal card
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry returns a warrant of correction, the statutory defect must be cured within the Korean court-stated grace period, normally two weeks, by filing a corrected exhibit and an explanatory note. If the defect is an insufficient capital deposit, a new deposit certificate is obtained and refiled. If the registration is dismissed, a fresh incorporation application may be refiled with corrected documentation; the company can also petition the district court for an adjudication reviewing the registry's rejection.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business Registration and Corporate Tax Identification with the National Tax Service
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local district tax office of the National Tax Service with jurisdiction over the registered head office; followed by municipal/provincial tax authority registration for local surtaxes
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the court registry issues the certificate of registered matters, the representative director or authorized agent must file a business registration application with the competent local tax office of the National Tax Service. The application must state the head-office address, business type as information and digital content production, actual business object, representative directors, and expected commencement date. The tax office will verify the court registration and issue a Business Registration Certificate assigning the company's corporate business registration number for corporate income tax, VAT, payroll withholding, and invoice issuance. The tax office then forwards registration data to local government for local income and property tax purposes. This step converts the legally incorporated entity into a fully operational and tax-compliant company.
required_dossiers: Business registration application form prescribed by the National Tax Service
Certificate of registered matters issued by the court registry
Certified copy of the notarized Articles of Incorporation
Identification card and alien registration where applicable for the representative director
Corporate seal certificate and seal specimen
Head-office lease contract or certificate of ownership
Bank deposit account details for tax refunds and national tax payments
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax office issues a request for clarification because the business classification does not align with the corporate object, the company files a formal correction letter with a revised business scope description emphasizing ISIC 5911 digital animation and CGI services. If the lease or head-office evidence is inadequate, the company submits a supplemental floor plan, utility contract, or rent receipt. The tax identification number is then issued after correction without resetting the SLA unless additional site inspection is ordered.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Governance Filings, Corporate Seal Reporting, and Operating Bank Account Activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Court Registry for corporate seal and representative director registration; National Tax Service for employee and business registration updates; domestic commercial bank for operating account opening
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Immediately after business registration, the board convenes a formal organizational board meeting and approves governance filings and banking mandates. The workflow requires: (i) filing the representative director and director registrations with the court registry, including the corporate seal report and specimen seal card; (ii) opening the company's permanent operating bank account, presenting the Business Registration Certificate, certificate of registered matters, corporate seal, representative director identification, and board resolution authorizing account opening; (iii) activating payment rails through Wise B2B and SWIFT wire with AML/KYC documentation for the underlying trade invoices; (iv) registering all employees and the work-site establishment with the National Tax Service and local branch of the National Pension Service and Korea Workers' Compensation & Welfare Service; and (v) adopting the company's bookkeeping and e-tax invoice system. This finalizes operational readiness for a digital 3D animation production company.
required_dossiers: Certificate of registered matters from the court registry
Business Registration Certificate from the National Tax Service
Corporate seal certificate and specimen seal
Representative director passport or alien registration card
Board resolution authorizing bank account opening and officers
AML/KYC forms, ultimate beneficial owner declaration, and company ownership chart
Employment registration forms and social insurance setup forms for Korean employees
E-tax invoice service registration confirmation and VAT filing mandate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank imposes enhanced due diligence because of foreign beneficial ownership or cross-border payment rails, the company provides an ultimate beneficial owner declaration backed by passport copies and corporate chain chart. If the registry raises any issue on the corporate seal or director registration, the representative director executes corrected seal report forms and refiles with the original court extract. If the National Tax Service rejects employee registration due to missing foreign employer codes, the payroll agent corrects the work-site registration and resubmits within one SLA day.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable — no industrial licensing board is engaged because the registered object is pure digital content production under ISIC 5911 and does not involve physical manufacturing, chemical processing, assembly, or warehousing activities within ISIC 1xxx, 2xxx, 3xxx, 4xxx, or 52xx.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable — no statutory industrial operating permit is required for commercial 3D animation and CGI visual effects production. The company is operational with the court issuance of the certificate of registered matters and the National Tax Service Business Registration Certificate. Age-rating classification by the Korea Media Rating Board, if a motion picture or video product is distributed, is a content rating determination, not an industrial operating license.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not Applicable — the Korean Ministry of Environment is not triggered because no site construction, land development, factory installation, or physical infrastructure project is involved in a pure 3D animation production operation.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt / Not Applicable — no EIA registration, environmental impact assessment report, or prior environmental consultation is required under the Korean Environmental Impact Assessment Act, because the activity is office-based digital content creation with zero physical development footprint.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable — no industrial wastewater discharge, no volatile organic compound emission, and no hazardous waste stream is generated by rendering, design, or software development. If general office electronics are eventually discarded, such equipment waste must be handled by licensed e-waste collectors under the Act on Control of Wastes; this is a general waste duty rather than a manufacturing discharge permit.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable — no Civil Defense fire permit, structural load clearance, or factory workplace safety approval is required because there is no industrial plant or warehouse. An ordinary office lease remains subject to general fire safety compliance under the Fire Services Act, including extinguishers, emergency exits, and fire alarms where required by building floor area, but this is not an industrial civil defense permit. Occupational safety obligations under the Occupational Safety and Health Act apply only to the ordinary office environment and only when hiring employees, with no special operating license triggered for digital production.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea; online electronic portal: Home Tax Service (HTS) at hometax.go.kr
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a newly formed Korean Chusik Hoesa, the statutory TIN is the 10-digit Business Registration Number (BRN). The representative director must submit a business registration application to the competent district NTS office within 20 days of the commencement of business, attaching the court-registered certificate of incorporation from the commercial registry, the articles of incorporation, identity documents of the directors, and proof of the registered office address. The NTS then issues the BRN certificate. For a foreign non-resident entity that has Korean VAT or withholding obligations but no domestic place of business, the entity must appoint a Korean tax representative (a resident individual or a domestic corporation) and file a simplified non-resident business registration through HTS or the competent tax office. Supporting documents include the home-country certificate of incorporation, apostilled or consular-legalized corporate documents, a board resolution appointing the tax representative, a power of attorney, and a statement describing the Korean-source supplies. For foreign suppliers of electronic services, the simplified e-service registration module of HTS must be used; after verification, the NTS assigns a 10-digit BRN and an electronic tax invoice issuance account. The tax representative is jointly responsible for registration, filing, and payment unless a physical Korean establishment is created.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation - A Korean Chusik Hoesa is classified as a domestic corporation taxable under the Corporate Tax Act on its worldwide income; it is not eligible for pass-through treatment. Korean-source income of a foreign non-resident owner remains separately subject to dividend withholding tax under Korean domestic law and applicable tax treaties.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None - Korean tax law does not provide U.S.-style check-the-box elections or hybrid mismatch elections. A Chusik Hoesa is per se an entity-level taxpayer. The only available relevant elections are (i) group consolidated corporate tax filing under the Corporate Tax Act for a domestic parent and 100-percent-owned domestic subsidiaries, and (ii) tax-neutral reorganization elections under the Corporate Tax Act and the Tax Incentive Limitation Act for qualifying mergers, divisions, and asset transfers.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the Korean Value-Added Tax Act
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general de minimis turnover threshold; VAT registration is mandatory from the first taxable supply in Korea (effectively KRW 0). Foreign non-resident electronic-service suppliers are subject to simplified registration through the Home Tax Service (HTS) portal.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Every VAT-registered business must issue a Korean Electronic Tax Invoice (ETI) through HTS or an NTS-certified e-invoicing solution for taxable supplies. The ETI must be transmitted to HTS within one business day after issuance. The system assigns a unique tax invoice number and performs automated cross-matching with monthly VAT returns, customs declaration data, and cash receipt records; this is an anti-fraud e-invoice clearance and matching regime rather than a fiscal digital-stamping model. Non-issuance, late issuance, or issuance of a false ETI triggers additional tax penalties of up to 2% of the supply value plus statutory surcharges.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: 0% VAT zero-rating is available for: (i) goods exported outside Korea and duly cleared by Korea Customs Service; (ii) services rendered or supplies made in a foreign country; (iii) foreign exchange-earning services, including commercial animation/VFX production and licensing of copyrights or characters to an overseas client, when the place of supply is outside Korea and the remuneration is paid in foreign currency; and (iv) services supplied for ships or aircraft in international navigation under the VAT Act. The taxpayer must prove actual delivery or performance outside Korea, collection of export proceeds in foreign currency, and record the transaction in the VAT export return. Qualifying zero-rated supplies generate input VAT credits and refunds through the periodic VAT return.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Korea Customs Service Export Declaration Certificate (Export Customs Clearance Certificate) for physical goods
Commercial invoice and detailed service contract / statement of work describing the animation or VFX deliverables
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill for the physical movement of media or assets
Inward Remittance Certificate (IRC) issued by a Korean authorized foreign-exchange bank proving foreign-currency receipt of the export purchase price
Foreign Currency Revenue Ledger and bank remittance advices evidencing collection within the statutory repatriation deadline
Digital delivery records, access logs, transfer logs, or overseas client acceptance/completion certificate for intangible or electronically delivered animation/VFX content
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export zero-rating is subject to NTS audit cross-checks against Korea Customs Service export declarations, HTS e-invoice records, foreign-exchange settlement records, and the taxpayer's books. If documentation is missing, the 0% rate is reversed and 10% VAT is assessed on the supply, together with additional tax for unfaithful returns (10% of the underreported or reclaimed tax, and 40% for fraudulent returns), plus monthly overdue interest. Proceeds not received within 180 days of export are treated as uncollected and the zero-rating is clawed back unless a banking extension is approved. Deliberate fake exports or false zero-rating claims may also be criminally prosecuted under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act, resulting in imprisonment and fines up to the statutory limits.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (The Central Bank of the Republic of Korea), operating with the Ministry of Economy and Finance as the responsible policy authority under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, South Korea maintains a comprehensively liberalized current account and a predominantly open capital account, yet all cross-border movements of funds must be handled indirectly through authorized domestic foreign exchange banks and disclosed through the Bank of Korea reporting system. The Korean won is freely convertible at onshore market rates for legitimate trade, investment, and financial transactions, but KRW is not a physically deliverable international currency outside approved regulated channels. Export proceeds are not subject to any mandatory surrender or conversion ratio; exporters may retain foreign currency balances in designated foreign exchange accounts or convert them as needed. Profit remittance hurdles for a fully compliant Chusik Hoesa are limited to corporate formalities: payment of corporate tax and withholding taxes where applicable, audited financial statements demonstrating distributable profits, a board of directors resolution declaring dividends, and a routine foreign exchange report filed with the receiving authorized bank. For a foreign-invested entity that completes the Foreign Investment Promotion Act registration, dividend and liquidation proceeds can be remitted freely once the capital verification and periodic tax filings are reconciled with the bank. The key practical obstacle is not convertibility but documentary completeness; banks require the full underlying corporate and transaction trail for every cross-border payment.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under current foreign exchange transaction regulations, an exporter must receive export proceeds in foreign currency through a domestic authorized foreign exchange bank within the statutory due date, generally within six months from the date of export declaration, unless an extension is approved by the bank or authorities for valid commercial reasons. There is no mandatory conversion ratio and no surrender obligation; the exporter may retain the foreign currency in a foreign currency current account, convert to Korean won at the prevailing market rate, or utilize the funds for permitted trade-related payments. Completed export proceeds must be reported for balance-of-payments statistical purposes, and supporting invoices, bills of lading, customs declarations, and settlement documents should be preserved for at least five years to satisfy auditing and banking review.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Basic Operational Currency Account with Foreign Investment Capital Facility
Capital Escrow Account and Basic Operational Currency Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-to-Negligible direct viability for unlicensed offshore digital EMIs. South Korea requires any electronic payment or money transfer service provider to be authorized or registered under the Electronic Financial Transactions Act, and cross-border remittance must be originated or received through a domestic foreign exchange bank. An offshore EMI such as a non-bank fintech cannot operate as a standalone corporate settlement account without a domestic banking license. It may be used only as a supplementary receivable channel where it routes funds through an authorized Korean bank, maintains transparent beneficiary disclosure, and is not the primary treasury rail. Any treasury structure that leaves the Chusik Hoesa reliant on an unlicensed EMI will create immediate AML, FX reporting, and tax audit exposure.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In-branch physical presence is the standard requirement for at least one statutory director and the ultimate beneficial owner at account opening. Remote video verification is generally not accepted for newly established corporate entities with foreign directors; consular proxy opening without the principal physically attending is not permitted as the sole completion method. A non-resident director must present a valid passport and, where applicable, a foreign residence certificate. For directors who cannot travel, an apostilled or consular-legalized power of attorney may allow them to be represented only for non-account-signatory administrative matters; the actual signatory should appear in person to satisfy the bank's explicit KYC interview mandate.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear beneficial ownership or opaque source-of-funds for the initial share capital and foreign investment remittance.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: For each shareholder, provide the beneficial ownership declaration form, corporate registry extract of any intermediate holding entities, bank-sourced remittance advice proving the exact funding trail, audited financial statements of significant shareholders, source-of-wealth statement, proof of residential and business address, the Foreign Investment Report certificate, and a detailed statement reconciling each capital remittance against bank receipts and the statutory capital ledger.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border B2B invoicing for 3D animation and VFX services that cannot demonstrate bona fide commercial substance, especially where invoice amounts are high relative to early-stage company financials.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed master service agreements with detailed statements of work, milestone delivery schedules, client acceptance certificates, asset handover logs, frame renders or automated VFX delivery manifests, prior payment ledgers, and the precise ISIC 5911 / NAICS 512110 service description encoded in invoice and remittance purpose documentation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Positive hits or ambiguous nexus to sanctions, politically exposed persons, restricted jurisdictions, or round-robin remittance patterns through shell-like intermediary accounts.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Passport copies of all directors and ultimate beneficial owners, personal background declarations, government-issued address verification, corporate registry extracts for counterparties, completed sanctions screening outputs, negative media search explanations, and a documented payment chain confirming that no transaction benefits a designated person or restricted regime.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Insufficient tax documentation and withholding compliance evidence during account periodic review, particularly for royalty or profit-sharing outflows.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Valid business registration certificate, corporate seal certificate, recent value-added tax filings with proof of payment, corporate tax payment receipts, absence of national tax delinquency certificate, tax representation appointment letter if a non-resident officer acts, and a formal withholding tax reconciliation schedule for any royalties or dividends paid to foreign parties.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The foreign shareholder must submit the Foreign Investment Report through a domestic authorized foreign exchange bank under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act before capital transmission. The remittance should be executed via SWIFT MT103 to the bank-designated foreign investment custody account, clearly stating the Korean entity legal name, business registration number, foreign investment declaration number, and capital purpose code corresponding to direct investment. Upon final collection, the bank converts the foreign currency into Korean won and credits the Chusik Hoesa's operational KRW account. The bank's foreign currency receipt confirmation, the exchange conversion slip, and a capital verification certification signed by an eligible Korean certified public accountant must be retained in the statutory accounting archive. Any shareholder loan or intra-group advance should be separately declared as intra-company financing under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Regulations and supported by a pre-executed loan agreement with market-conforming maturity and interest.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For high-value international subcontracting in visual effects and animation, the preferred clearing rail is SWIFT MT103 with full underlying contract reference, because it provides direct, irrevocable, and traceable settlement. Commercial letters of credit are acceptable when the debtor needs bank payment assurance, especially for larger licensing deals or co-production milestones, but require exact compliance with UCP600 documentation. Documentary collections are appropriate for routine supplier payments at lower risk where the creditor accepts delayed settlement. All outbound foreign currency disbursements must be accompanied by a tax invoice, a customs declaration where goods are involved, a withholding tax certificate for royalties and service fees, and the relevant foreign exchange bank filing.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable foreign exchange forward contracts with authorized Korean commercial banks, strictly limited to hedged commercial underlying exposures
Non-deliverable forward (NDF) contracts via offshore counterparties for KRW risk management when the onshore forward cannot be perfected
Plain-vanilla currency options transacted through authorized Korean banks with premium settlement and documentary proof of underlying exposure
Cross-currency swaps between Korean won and USD or EUR for long-term contractual revenue streams, subject to Bank of Korea reporting and commercial-event documentation

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Regular Annual General Meeting of Shareholders and Approval of Annual Financial Statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders' Meeting of the Chusik Hoesa; minutes and financial statements maintained at the registered corporate seat; no filing fee is payable to a government registry merely for holding the meeting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after the close of the fiscal year; for a calendar-year company by no later than 31 March
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No strike-off is directly linked to the AGM, but each director or officer in wilful default is subject to administrative fines of up to KRW 5,000,000 under Article 635 of the Korean Commercial Act; failure to hold the AGM may also expose the company to FSS designation for compulsory external audit and to civil liability of the directors.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return, including Local Income Tax Reconciliation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) for national corporate tax; the local government having jurisdiction over the place of corporate tax payment for the local income tax
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By 31 March of the following year for a calendar-year company; if the return is prepared and signed by a certified tax accountant, the deadline is extended to 30 April
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: The NTS imposes late-filing surcharges of up to 20% of the unpaid tax and statutory late-payment surcharges calculated daily under the Framework Act on National Taxes; enforced collection may include seizure of bank accounts and receivables, and repeated failure can cause administrative investigation and, for inactive or dormant companies, administrative closure or dissolution by the competent government body.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: External Audit Report Filing under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) and Financial Services Commission through the Data Analysis, Retrieval and Transfer System (DART)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within the DART filing window applicable under the External Audit Act, in practice within two to three weeks after the regular general meeting that approves the audited financial statements; for a calendar-year company with a March AGM, typically by mid-April
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: The FSS can issue corrective orders and administrative fines with statutory ceilings of up to KRW 30,000,000 for repeated non-compliance, publicly disclose the violation, and in serious cases recommend the appointment of a statutory auditor; this does not by itself strike off the company but can lead to restriction on reliance on the financial statements and to prosecution under the External Audit Act.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Shareholder Register and Corporate Secretarial Register Audit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Board of Directors of the Chusik Hoesa, recorded in board minutes; not filed with a public registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Prior to the annual general meeting and in any event by the AGM statutory deadline of 31 March for calendar-year companies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No external penalty attaches, but an uncured register defect restricts share-transfer recognition, impairs the directors' responsibility declaration, and may lead to administrative fines if the shareholder register is not properly kept as required by the Korean Commercial Act.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Foreign Investment Alteration Report, if the Company Is a Foreign-Invested Enterprise
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economy and Finance / Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA) through the receiving bank or KOTRA office that accepted the original foreign investment report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days from the date of any share transfer, share subscription, capital increase or reduction, disposal, or withdrawal that changes the foreign investment registration; if no such event occurs, no annual UBO renewal filing is required solely for maintenance of a non-listed Chusik Hoesa
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to report an alteration or under-reporting can result in administrative fines under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, loss of foreign-invested enterprise benefits and tax incentives, and possible restrictions on dividend and capital remittance benefits; it is not a corporate strike-off trigger unless the company becomes a wholly inactive registered entity.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Independent CPA audit is mandatory under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies when the balance-sheet total assets of the Chusik Hoesa at the immediately preceding fiscal year-end equal or exceed KRW 12,000,000,000, approximately USD 8.8 to 9.3 million depending on exchange rate, or when the company is a listed or public-interest company, is subject to consolidated external audit as a parent or subsidiary of a publicly accountable group, or is expressly designated by the FSS for investor protection. Turnover and headcount do not create a statutory audit obligation in the Republic of Korea; the applicable test is based on total assets and public-interest character. K-GAAP small-company relief and limited-review provisions may apply only within the narrow SME asset corridors permitted by the External Audit Act.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24% top marginal rate under Corporate Tax Act Article 55: 9% on taxable income up to KRW 200 million, 19% on KRW 200 million to 20 billion, 21% on KRW 20 billion to 300 billion, and 24% above KRW 300 billion.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general tax holiday; available incentives include R&D tax credit for qualified digital content/3D animation technology under the Restriction of Special Taxation Act, SME preferential rates, job-creation tax credit, and free economic zone / foreign investment zone income tax reductions under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act; no Korean patent box applies.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Income Tax Return for corporations prescribed under the Corporate Tax Act, together with the foreign corporation supplementary schedule; filed electronically through the National Tax Service HomeTax portal under the corporation's tax registration number.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual, with a semi-annual interim tax prepayment declaration after the first six months of the fiscal year.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The final annual return is due within 3 months following the close of the fiscal year; for a calendar-year corporation the deadline is March 31. The interim declaration is due within 2 months after the end of each 6-month block of the fiscal year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name of the Chusik Hoesa, business registration number, representative director, registered address, principal business code (ISIC 5911 / NAICS 512110), fiscal year start and end, and declaration of domestic or foreign corporation status.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If any shareholder is non-resident, attach an ownership schedule; if the entity is a foreign corporation with a Korean permanent establishment, enter the PE registration number and Korean place of business; if no Korean PE exists, mark the return as a Foreign Corporation Return and restrict income to Korean-source passive income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net income before corporate tax per Korean tax-adjusted financial statements, presenting revenue from 3D animation production, VFX service contracts, royalties, and licensing fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident PEs must record only Korean-source income attributable to the PE; from Box 2 onward all foreign-origin revenue is reversed; recognize revenue on completion of animation milestones and adjust foreign exchange differences where payments are received through Wise B2B or SWIFT wire.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Add back non-deductible entertainment expenses, penalties, excess officer compensation, and reserves; subtract non-taxable income and statutory deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Transfer pricing adjustments must be added to taxable income if a related-party intercompany contract is repriced by the National Tax Service; apply the Korean thin-capitalization and interest deductibility limits to any shareholder debt before entering this box.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 4 (Loss Carryforward Deduction and Tax Base)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deduct prior-year operating losses within the statutory carryforward period and apply special deductions to arrive at the corporate tax base.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only Korean PE trading income may utilize NOL carryforwards; a foreign corporation cannot shelter home-office losses against Korean profits; attach a loss carryforward schedule; for a domestic Chusik Hoesa, the 10-year carryforward applies.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5 (Gross Corporate Tax and Progressive Rates)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Calculate gross national corporate tax by applying the statutory progressive rate brackets to the tax base; where shown, enter the 10% local income tax surtax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a foreign corporation with a Korean PE, calculate national corporate tax on Korean PE profits and compute any branch profit remittance tax separately on post-tax profits to be remitted offshore; do not treat such remittance tax as a dividend deduction or as foreign tax credit on the same return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 6 (Tax Credits, Prepayments, and Withholding Relief)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter foreign tax credits, R&D credits, taxes withheld at source, interim tax prepayments, and any refund claimed.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the Korean entity paid dividends, royalties, or interest to non-residents at a treaty-reduced rate, attach the Tax Residency Certificate, beneficial ownership declaration, and NTS approval; if the full 22% was over-withheld, claim the refund in this box; failure to reconcile brings interest charges.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 7 (International Related-Party Transactions and Transfer Pricing Schedule)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclosure schedule for all cross-border related-party payments, including VFX subcontracts, character IP royalties, management charges, and intercompany loans, with pricing method selected and arm's-length margin.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Mandatory when related-party transactions exceed KRW 5 billion; for the 3D animation business, include character IP licensing flows, animation studio service charges, and profit attributed to offshore distribution entities; NTS may reject or audit the return if documentation is incomplete.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers an unfaithful-return additional tax of 20% of the unpaid tax (10% if a corrected return is filed), a delayed-payment additional tax of 0.025% per day, and NTS collection measures including asset seizure and travel blacklisting; intentional fraudulent returns are referred under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act for criminal fines and imprisonment.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 20% Korean national withholding tax plus 10% local surtax on that national tax, resulting in a 22% aggregate statutory withholding rate; DTA may reduce the rate to 5%, 10%, or 15% depending on the recipient and shareholding.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Before the distribution, the payer and recipient must file an application through HomeTax under the relevant DTA, attaching a current Tax Residency Certificate issued by the residence state, evidence of beneficial ownership and substantive business operations, shareholding records for the rate tier, and a board resolution authorizing the dividend, royalty, or interest; the withholding agent must retain the approved application and supporting documents for at least five years; if treaty relief is not pre-approved, the full 22% is withheld and a refund claim may be submitted within the statutory limitation period.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties for IP, copyrights, 3D animation, and content licenses: statutory 20% national plus 2% local surtax = 22% aggregate; intercompany interest: statutory 20% plus 2% = 22% aggregate; an applicable DTA may lower royalties to 15% or less and interest to 10% to 15%, but only where the recipient is the beneficial owner, performs real economic activity, and does not have a Korean permanent establishment attributable to the income.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: KRW 5 billion in annual related-party international transactions triggers the Local File; KRW 100 billion group revenue combined with KRW 5 billion related-party transactions triggers the Master File; consolidated group revenue of KRW 1 trillion triggers Country-by-Country Reporting.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Korea does not maintain UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations, but the Korean General Anti-Abuse Rule, substance-over-form jurisprudence, and the OECD BEPS Principal Purpose Test require economic activity and business purpose; NTS will disregard a conduit or letter-box company lacking employees, premises, decision-making functions, and core income-generating activities, and will deny treaty benefits where the structure is artificial.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Beneficial Ownership / Treaty Shopping / Letter-Box Company
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Routing 3D animation licensing profits into a no-substance intermediary in a low-tax jurisdiction solely to claim treaty withholding reductions on dividends, royalties, or interest paid through the intermediary.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty benefits under Article 17 of the International Tax Adjustment Act and the OECD Multilateral Instrument Principal Purpose Test; recharacterization of the intermediary as a sham; additional tax of up to 20% of the understated withholding tax plus 0.025% daily late payment surcharge; the payer is jointly held to the unpaid withholding obligation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who authorized sham documentation are personally liable for the corporation's unpaid withholding tax under the National Tax Collection Act; personal assets may be seized; a travel ban and NTS blacklisting apply; criminal referral under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act may result in imprisonment for up to five years for intentional tax evasion.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Fraud and Thin Capitalization
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Undercharging a related offshore studio for VFX rendering or overpaying intellectual property royalties to shift Korean profit; failing to prepare or attach the Local File and Master File after the KRW 5 billion related-party threshold; applying fabricated margins to intercompany transactions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: NTS redetermines taxable income under the arm's length standard in the International Tax Adjustment Act and disallows excessive interest under thin-capitalization rules; assessment plus an unfaithful-return penalty of up to 20% of omitted tax, daily interest, and separate penalty for non-production of transfer-pricing documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: If the corporation cannot pay, directors who directed false transfer-pricing data are secondarily liable for the assessed tax; personal real estate may be attached; overseas travel restriction is imposed; criminal indictment for false document creation and tax evasion may carry imprisonment for up to five years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Unreported Offshore Profit Repatriation / Foreign Exchange Evasion
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Placing royalty or license fees in an offshore Wise B2B or SWIFT account without declaring the foreign exchange transaction and without including the income in the Korean corporate return, then using the offshore balance as a hidden dividend or personal reimbursement.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, unauthorized transfer of Korean profits abroad can attract imprisonment for up to five years or a fine up to five times the amount involved; the National Tax Service imposes a 20% understatement penalty and unpaid withholding on unreported dividends, plus statutory interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: A court may pierce the corporate veil because the offshore account was used as an alter ego; directors are jointly and severally liable for restitution to creditors and NTS; passport revocation, travel ban, asset freezing, confiscation of hidden funds, and imprisonment for up to five years for tax evasion apply.
